typical_data_frame_transmit_sequence: 1. Wait for bus idle (≥ 11 consecutive recessive bits).
2. Drive START OF FRAME (1 dominant bit); all nodes hard-synchronize.
3. Drive 11-bit IDENTIFIER + RTR bit (ARBITRATION FIELD); on each bit monitor bus level. If drove recessive but bus is dominant → LOSE arbitration, withdraw, become receiver of the winner's frame.
5. Drive DATA FIELD (0..8 bytes, MSB first per byte).
6. Drive 15-bit CRC SEQUENCE + recessive CRC DELIMITER.
7. Drive recessive ACK SLOT; sample bus; expect dominant ACK from at least one receiver. Otherwise raise ACKNOWLEDGMENT ERROR.
8. Drive recessive ACK DELIMITER + 7 recessive END OF FRAME bits.
10. (if error-passive) Drive 8 recessive SUSPEND TRANSMISSION bits before next transmission.
typical_remote_frame_sequence: 1. Send DATA FRAME structure with RTR = recessive and no DATA FIELD.
2. Node holding the matching DATA FRAME responds with DATA FRAME (same IDENTIFIER).
3. If a DATA FRAME and matching REMOTE FRAME start simultaneously, DATA FRAME wins (RTR dominant beats RTR recessive).
typical_receive_sequence: 1. Receiver detects SOF dominant bit; hard-synchronizes.
2. Sample IDENTIFIER + RTR (or RRS in FD) + IDE.
3. At FDF bit: dominant → Classical path; recessive → FD path.
4. (FD) Detect res bit: if res = 1 → Protocol Exception.
5. (FD) Detect BRS bit: if BRS = 1 → switch to DBTP.
6. Receive DATA FIELD + CRC + (ISO FD) stuff-count parity.
7. (FD with BRS = 1) At CRC delimiter: switch back to NBTP.
8. If CRC matched: drive dominant ACK on ACK SLOT.
9. Apply Acceptance Filter; write Rx FIFO / Rx Buffer element.
arbitration_loss_sequence: 1. Two transmitters start simultaneously on bus idle.
2. On each ARBITRATION FIELD bit, each compares its driven bit to bus.
3. The first time a transmitter drives recessive but reads dominant: it loses arbitration.
4. Loser withdraws (stops driving) and becomes a receiver of the winner's frame.
5. Loser may retry retransmission once the bus is idle again.
error_signalling_sequence: 1. Error-active node detects BIT/STUFF/FORM/ACK error during a frame.
2. At the next bit, transmit ACTIVE ERROR FLAG (6 dominant bits).
3. Other nodes detect this and transmit their own ACTIVE ERROR FLAG; superposition results in 6..12 dominant bits.
4. After ERROR FLAG, transmit ERROR DELIMITER (8 recessive bits).
5. Original transmitter automatically retransmits the message once bus is idle.
6. CRC errors specifically: ERROR FLAG starts at the bit following ACK DELIMITER (not immediately).
fault_confinement_transition_sequence: 1. error-active → error-passive: when TX_ERR_COUNT ≥ 128 or RX_ERR_COUNT ≥ 128.
3. error-passive → error-active: when both TX_ERR_COUNT and RX_ERR_COUNT ≤ 127.
4. bus-off → error-active: after observing 128 consecutive sequences of 11 recessive bits; both error counts reset to 0.
wake_up_sequence: 1. Node enters sleep mode: internal activity stopped; bus drivers disconnected.
2. Bus activity (any dominant edge) or internal condition triggers wake-up.
3. Transfer layer waits for oscillator to stabilize.
4. Waits for 11 consecutive recessive bits → confirmed bus synchronization.
6. To wake other nodes: transmit special wake-up message with identifier 'rrr rrrd rrrr' (the lowest possible priority — guaranteed to lose arbitration to anything else).
software_initialization_sequence: 1. After hardware reset, CCCR.INIT = 1; m_can_tx = recessive.
2. Set CCCR.CCE = 1 to enable write access.
3. Initialize Message RAM (write 0x0 to each word) if ECC enabled.
8. Program CCCR: NISO, TXP, EFBI, PXHD, WMM, UTSU, BRSE, FDOE, DAR.
9. Program TSCC, TOCC, IE, ILS, ILE, TXBTIE, TXBCIE.
12. BSP waits for 11 consecutive recessive bits before joining bus.
typical_classical_data_frame_transmit_se: 3. M_CAN Tx Handler scans Tx Buffers + updates TXBRP.TRP_n.
9. Drive recessive ACK SLOT; sample bus.
typical_can_fd_data_frame_transmit_seque: 1..3. Same as Classical but T1.FDF = 1 + BRS = 1.
6a. Drive r1 + FDF=1 + res + BRS=1 at NBTP rate.
6b. At BRS bit sample point: switch to DBTP. ESI + DLC at DBTP.
7. Drive DATA FIELD (0..64 bytes) at DBTP.
8b. Drive CRC17 or CRC21 at DBTP.
9. At CRC DELIMITER: switch back to NBTP.
13. (T1.EFC = 1) Write Tx Event FIFO with FDF + BRS = 1.
Same as classical except T1.FDF = 1, BRS = 0. Whole frame at NBTP rate; CAN FD CRC; RRS replaces RTR.
typical_remote_frame_sequence_classical_: 1. Host writes Tx Buffer T0.RTR = 1, T1.FDF = 0, T1.DLC = 0.
2. M_CAN transmits Classical remote frame even if CCCR.FDOE = 1.
3. Node holding matching DATA FRAME responds.
4. DATA wins over REMOTE on simultaneous start.
tx_event_handling_sequence: 2. If T1.EFC = 1, write Tx Event FIFO at TXEFS.EFPI.
5. Host reads element at EFGI; writes TXEFA.EFAI.
transmit_cancellation_sequence: 1. Host writes TXBCR.CR_n = 1 (dedicated or Queue only).
2. If not yet started: TXBRP.TRP_n cleared; TXBCF.CF_n set.
3. If ongoing: cancellation finishes on success / disturbance.
5. DAR mode + success-in-spite-of-cancel: Tx Event with ET = 10.
power_down_sequence: 1. CPU asserts m_can_clkstop_req or sets CCCR.CSR = 1.
2. M_CAN completes pending Tx + waits for Bus_Idle.
tdc_per_frame_sequence_with_BRS: 2. At FDF → res falling edge on m_can_tx, start delay counter.
3. Stop when same edge seen on m_can_rx.
6. Use SSP for bit-error check in data phase.
acceptance_filter_sequence_for_high_prio: 3. Match: update HPMS register with FLST/FIDX/MSI/BIDX.
5. Host CPU reads HPMS, fast-paths the message.
debug_on_can_dma_sequence: 1. Configure 3 filter elements with SFEC/EFEC = 111 + SFID2/EFID2[10:9] = 01 (A), 10 (B), 11 (C).
2. Configure 3 consecutive Rx Buffers for A/B/C.
